subject: EchoHealth discovery — latency, throughput, and deployment topology

Subject: EchoHealth discovery — latency, throughput, and deployment topology

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick written summary so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I kept this tight; please flag any corrections.

Key pain points you called out:
- Tail latency variability at peak (spiky queries during morning triage window) — 99th percentile occasionally breaches 400–500ms for short prompts.
- Cost sensitivity for batching-heavy endpoints that drive daily summaries (need predictable unit economics).
- Data governance: PHI in prompts, requirement for customer-managed keys and private networking.

High-level goals we heard:
- Target 99th percentile latency <= 150ms for single-turn triage prompts (~75–150 tokens typical).
- Sustained throughput target of ~450–600 requests/sec during peak; burst to 1k RPS for 30–45s tolerable with autoscale.
- Private deployment or VPC peering for PHI workloads; audit logs & KMS/HSM integration mandatory.

Model/quality constraints you emphasized:
- Prefer open / audited family (Llama2-13B or similar) if cost/throughput tradeoffs are favorable; acceptable to run a quantized 13B or a performant 30B variant if latency/quality justify it.
- Deterministic-ish outputs for downstream classification (we noted evaluation harness + unit prompts).

Initial topology considerations (what we recommended in call):
- Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with a small warm standby across us-east-1 for failover.
- Autoscale policy tuned for steady-state concurrency with short, conservative scale-up to prevent cold-start tail spikes.
- KV/prefix caching at the request-router level for repeated triage templates to shave token generation.
- Private control plane + VPC peering; customer KMS for key management.

Open questions / asks for EchoHealth before we size:
1) Typical prompt length distribution (p50/p95 token counts) for triage vs long-summary endpoints (if you can paste a small sample sanitized set).
2) Expected concurrency per endpoint (how many concurrent users per region during your morning peak).
3) Any hard constraints on residency (must stay in us-west-2 only?) and procurement timeline.

Next steps / owners:
- Samira: share anonymized prompt samples and approximate daily request shape (p50, p95, hourly distribution).
- Marissa: will draft a recommended topology (VM/GPU type, quantization profile, and latency projection) and share by Wed EOD.
- Karthik: I'll compile commercial options (Dedicated vs Private) and an initial cost projection for the two targeted SLO tiers.

Attachments: attached sample SLO table and a template we use for prompt capture.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Thanks Karthik — this aligns well with what we discussed. Quick clarifications and added context:

Clarifications from our side:
- Token distribution (sanitized): triage prompts: p50=56, p95=128; long-summary jobs: p50=420, p95=1,200 (those are async and can be batched).
- Concurrency: peak morning triage window ~ 480 RPS sustained for 10–15 minutes; several thousand short bursts distributed across users (we approximate burst concurrency of ~950).
- Residency: must remain within US regions only; primary preference us-west-2.
- Compliance: SOC2 in place; we will need a Hosted or Private deployment with customer-managed KMS for PHI. HSM availability is a plus but not mandatory day 1.

Hard constraints/priority ranking:
1) Latency SLO for triage UI (user-facing) is top priority — <=150ms 99th is our stretch goal, 200ms acceptable as baseline.
2) Throughput predictability for cost forecasting is next.
3) Async long-summary quality > latency — willing to trade time for better model if cost-effective.

I've attached a spreadsheet with hourly qps and the sanitized prompt samples (see attachments). We can also loop procurement if you need formal RFP language — I'll CC them on the next note.

Appreciate the data, Samira — useful. I sketched a conservative technical plan below based on the SLOs and token profile you provided. Notes are intentionally pragmatic (we'll refine with telemetry once we have a test corpus).

Summary plan (short):
- Primary: Dedicated pool (reserved) in us-west-2 using A10G-equivalent GPUs (or latest gen we have in dedicated) with 8–12 instances depending on model and quantization. Warm standby in us-east-1 for failover and peak overflow.
- Model choices: start with Llama2-13B (int8/qat) for triage UI — it hits a good latency/price sweet spot and is compatible with prefix caching. For long summaries, run a higher-capacity variant (Llama2-70B q4 or a 30B float variant) on a separate pool with batched async workers.
- Caching/batching: enable prefix KV caching for triage templates (expected 20–30% token savings p95) and dynamic batching tuned to keep tail latency within SLO. We recommend a target batch size cap of ~48 for triage to balance latency and throughput.
- Autoscaling: predictive scale policy that reacts to moving-average of RPS with a short fast path for spikes (scale quickly to a limited burst capacity, then ramp to steady-state). This reduces cold-start risk.
- Networking: VPC peering + internal private link for request ingress; control plane stays private for your account. We'll enable customer KMS integration and can support HSM-backed keys in phase 2.
- Observability: token-level breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and anomaly alerts; we'll provide dashboards and alert thresholds you can tweak.

Quick projected numbers (VERY rough initial sizing):
- Triage (Llama2-13B int8): 10 A10G-equivalent instances ~= 550 sustained RPS with 99th ~120–180ms depending on prompt mix and caching; burst headroom to ~1k RPS with autoscale.
- Long-summary pool (30B quantized): 6 instances with aggressive batching to meet throughput; tail latency will be higher but run async.

Action items I can take this week:
- Produce a short runbook with expected latencies & cost buckets for the 13B vs 30B choices (by Thu EOD).
- Stand up a short PoC plan (1–2 week) to validate p95/p99 with your sanitized corpus; scope and prerequisites included.

Questions for EchoHealth:
- Are you comfortable sanitizing a 24–48 hour sample including timestamps and basic meta so we can mimic arrival patterns?
- Do you prefer the PoC in Dedicated (reserved) or Redwood Private? We'll price both but the lead time differs.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
